summary: Benton County, OR summit lookout: temporary tower and crew cabin 1942, three-level aluminum tower 1950, removed 1974; no site description found.

facts.design: Three-level tower: garage on the ground floor, crew quarters above, 14x14-ft glass lookout on top; aluminum (1950 accounts)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1974 per the register and Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com says destroyed. No later description of the site found

events.note: Five-man emergency crew stationed at the peak once an 18x28-ft cabin was finished
18 x 28 ft cabin completed; the district warden said a temporary 30-ft tower would be built
Lookout Anthony Kelly on duty; short-wave radio stolen from the tower in August 1947 (a February 1951 article says it was two years earlier)
Three-level aluminum tower completed early in the season; the register dates it to 1951
Vandals smashed a window and left newspapers burning inside; $50 reward offered
Station was first to spot four fires during the fire season
Removed per the register and Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com says destroyed

corrections.why: A 1950 Capital Journal item gives the planned height as 40 feet (12.2 m) with three levels. 4.3 m matches no source read. The 40 ft is a plan, not a measured height, so the editor should confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The August 15, 1947 Gazette-Times item dates the theft to 1947. A February 28, 1951 Gazette-Times item quotes Curtis saying the radio was stolen two years earlier. The story uses 1947 and states the conflict.

The register and firelookout.com date the tower to 1951. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1950 Forest Log item saying an aluminum lookout house was completed early in the season, and a February 1951 article saying the station was built last year. The story reports 1950 and notes the register's 1951.
The register and Forest Lookouts say removed in 1974; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1974. The story says removed and notes the other word.
Newspaper items place the lookout six miles west of Monroe, northwest of Monroe, west of Dawson, and west of Bellfountain. The register's coordinates are kept, and the story notes the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 4.3 is proposed as 12.2 from a 1950 plan; please confirm, since no measured height was found. The register and Forest Lookouts disagree on the build year (1951 vs 1950), and the story reports both. The Feb 1951 article says the radio was stolen 'two years ago', while the August 1947 article dates the theft; the story uses 1947 and states the conflict. The Forest Lookouts page is long and was read by grep, so later 1950s-1970s entries could be missed. Oregon newspaper archives (oregonnews.uoregon.edu) were not searched for the 1974 removal. Access and staffing after 1974 are not stated in any source and are left out. No photos found.
